definition: A cyberattack where an attacker secretly intercepts and potentially alters communications between two parties who believe they are communicating directly with each other.
metaDescription: Learn about man-in-the-middle attacks, how cybercriminals intercept communications, and ways to protect yourself from this privacy threat.
simpleExplanation: Imagine you're passing notes to a friend, but someone sits between you and secretly reads or changes your messages before passing them along. A man-in-the-middle attack works the same way with digital communications.
whyItMatters: These attacks can steal sensitive information like passwords, credit card numbers, or personal messages. They're particularly dangerous because victims often don't realize their communications are being intercepted and monitored.
technicalDetail: MITM attacks typically exploit vulnerabilities in network protocols or use techniques like ARP spoofing, DNS hijacking, or rogue Wi-Fi hotspots. Attackers position themselves between the victim and intended destination, often using packet sniffing tools to capture and analyze traffic before forwarding it to maintain the illusion of normal communication.

examples.explanation: An attacker creates a fake Wi-Fi hotspot called 'Free Airport WiFi' and intercepts all internet traffic from users who connect to it, stealing login credentials and personal data.
A cybercriminal intercepts emails between a customer and their bank, modifying account numbers in payment instructions to redirect money to their own account.
An attacker redirects traffic from a legitimate banking website to an identical fake site, capturing login credentials when users enter their information.
